solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

R068-01.notes: P2 says the silence frames sounds concertgoers were trained to ignore; P5 says the change in attention may be what Cage was after. A reverses the passage: Cage insisted it was NOT a joke, and he admitted nothing. B contradicts the passage, which treats whether it counts as music as an open question, and the piece contains no notes. D's 'first ever' claim appears nowhere.

R068-02.notes: P1 says the movements were 'marked by opening and closing the lid.' D is the stopwatch trap: he started it, and the passage never says he turned it on and off. B is wrong because he played nothing. C, announcing each movement, is not mentioned.

R068-03.notes: P2 lists the audience talking and walking out among the sounds the silence framed. A assumes silence was the goal, which Cage denied. B is wrong because Cage said it was never a joke. C has no support in the passage.

R068-04.notes: P3 opens 'Cage had come to this view partly through an experience' and tells the anechoic chamber story. A is too narrow: the chamber is described in only one clause. C is the subject of P1-P2, not P3. D is the subject of P4.

R068-05.notes: The engineer said the sounds were Cage's nervous system and his blood, which C paraphrases as 'his own body.' A is not stated. B is not stated, and the room absorbs sound. D: the engineer only explained the sounds; he did not make them.

R068-06.notes: In the chamber Cage still heard his own body, so a living listener always hears some sound. B contradicts 'does not exist.' C is wrong because the chamber did absorb outside sound. D, a dislike of silence, is not discussed.

R068-07.notes: P4 sets 'a philosophical statement more than a musical work' against 'a genuine composition.' A, B and C are details or matters the critics do not dispute. The passage says it has three movements, and the critics never address performer or venue.

R068-08.notes: P5 says both views miss 'the piece's quietest achievement,' a change in how listeners attend. A is wrong because the author never calls it a joke. C misreads the paragraph, which says both views miss something, not that both are correct. D: neither the author nor the critics tie their views to the 1952 performance details.

R068-09.notes: The silence 'frames' sounds people usually ignore, meaning it sets them off for attention. B is the literal picture-frame sense and the intended trap. C is the 'frame someone' sense. D is the 'frame a question' sense. Only A fits the context of drawing attention.

R068-10.notes: At five minutes the rereaders remembered slightly more, so a researcher testing only then would wrongly favor rereading, and the one-week result shows that is a mistake. B is the correct one-week conclusion, which that researcher could not have reached. C comes from Ebbinghaus in P1, not from this test. D reverses the confidence finding: the rereaders were the more confident group.
